summary: Any person that maintains or possesses consumer-report information for a business purpose must take reasonable measures when disposing of it.
applies_to: Employers, staffing firms and landlords that use background/consumer reports, plus their disposal vendors.

summary: Standalone written disclosure and authorization before procuring a consumer report for employment, plus pre-adverse and adverse action notices.
applies_to: Staffing agencies, PEOs and employers procuring background reports.

summary: Retain I-9s (identity-document data) for 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, whichever is later; recruiters/referrers for a fee have separate retention rules.
applies_to: All employers, including staffing agencies; recruiters/referrers for a fee.

summary: Firms that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI for a covered entity must meet the Security Rule directly, sign BAAs, and report breaches to the covered entity.
applies_to: Service firms handling PHI: law firms, CPAs/auditors, IT/MSPs, billing firms, call centers, staffing firms placing clinical staff, and similar.

summary: Consent, Do-Not-Call, autodialer/prerecorded-call restrictions and call-abandonment and recordkeeping rules. These are privacy-of-contact obligations for outbound call centers.

citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
summary: 12 requirement families for protecting cardholder data; enforced through card-brand and acquirer contracts.
applies_to: Any merchant or service provider that stores, processes or transmits payment card data.
size_thresholds: Validation level (SAQ vs. QSA ROC) depends on annual card-transaction volume under card-brand merchant-level programs. Those levels are set by the card brands and were not verified here.
status: v4.0.1 published June 11, 2024 (PCI SSC blog). Not a law. Check for any later revision.

summary: 15 basic safeguarding controls for contractor systems that process, store or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI).
applies_to: Federal contractors and subcontractors at any tier whose systems may hold FCI.
size_thresholds: No size threshold. Does not apply to acquisitions solely of COTS items (FAR 4.1902).
status: In force (clause dated NOV 2021). FAR CUI proposed rule (Jan 15, 2025) and FAR cyber incident reporting proposed rule (Oct 3, 2023) remain proposed. A 'Revolutionary FAR Overhaul' proposed rule was published June 23, 2026.

short_name: NYC Local Law 144 (Automated Employment Decision Tools)
citation: NYC Admin. Code 20-870 et seq. (Local Law 144 of 2021)
summary: Employers and employment agencies may not use an AEDT unless it has had a bias audit within one year, a summary of results is posted, and required notices are given.
applies_to: Employers and employment agencies (staffing firms) using AEDTs for NYC candidates/employees.

summary: Security plan with risk assessment, personnel security, unauthorized-access and en-route security measures. Physical/personnel focus rather than cyber.
applies_to: Persons offering or transporting the hazardous materials listed in 172.800 (e.g., hazardous waste haulers above the listed quantities).
size_thresholds: Applicability depends on the material/quantity thresholds in 49 CFR 172.800 (not itemized here).
